title: Count to Ten
description: Learn the basics of for loops by counting from 1 to 10.
instructions: Create a function called `solution()` that returns an array containing numbers from 1 to 10.
hints: Use a for loop that starts at 1 and goes to 10
Create an empty array before the loop: const result = []
Inside the loop, use result.push(i) to add each number
Don't forget to return the result array
Solution: Use for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) with array.push()

title: Sum of Array
description: Use a loop to calculate the sum of all numbers in an array.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(numbers)` that takes an array of numbers and returns their sum.
hints: Create a variable to accumulate the sum, starting at 0
Loop through each element in the array
Use numbers.length to know how many items to loop through
Add each number to your sum: sum += numbers[i]
Solution: let sum = 0; for loop with sum += numbers[i]

title: Count Even Numbers
description: Count how many even numbers are in an array.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(numbers)` that counts and returns how many even numbers are in the array.
hints: Create a counter variable starting at 0
Loop through each number in the array
Use the modulo operator (%) to check if a number is even
If a number is even, increment your counter
Solution: count++ when numbers[i] % 2 === 0

title: Reverse an Array
description: Create a reversed copy of an array using a loop.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(arr)` that returns a new array with elements in reverse order.
hints: Start from the last index: arr.length - 1
Loop backwards: i-- instead of i++
Stop when i reaches 0 (use i >= 0)
Push each element to a new array
Solution: for (let i = arr.length - 1; i >= 0; i--)

title: Find Maximum
description: Find the largest number in an array using a loop.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(numbers)` that returns the largest number in the array.
hints: Start by assuming the first element is the maximum
Loop through the rest of the array
Compare each element to your current maximum
Update the maximum if you find a larger number
Solution: let max = numbers[0]; if (numbers[i] > max) max = numbers[i]

title: Multiply Array Elements
description: Create a new array with each element multiplied by a given factor.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(numbers, factor)` that returns a new array with each number multiplied by the factor.
hints: Create an empty result array
Loop through each number
Multiply each number by the factor
Push the result to your new array
Solution: result.push(numbers[i] * factor)

title: Filter Positive Numbers
description: Extract only positive numbers from an array.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(numbers)` that returns a new array containing only the positive numbers (greater than 0).
hints: Create an empty result array
Loop through each number
Check if the number is greater than 0
If positive, add it to the result array
Solution: if (numbers[i] > 0) result.push(numbers[i])

title: Repeat String
description: Use a loop to repeat a string multiple times.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(str, times)` that returns the string repeated the specified number of times.
hints: Start with an empty string: let result = ''
Loop the specified number of times
In each iteration, add the string to your result
Use the += operator to concatenate strings
Solution: result += str inside the loop

title: Fibonacci Sequence
description: Generate the first N numbers of the Fibonacci sequence.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(n)` that returns an array containing the first n Fibonacci numbers (starting with 0, 1).
hints: The Fibonacci sequence starts with [0, 1]
Each next number is the sum of the previous two
Start with an array containing [0, 1]
Use a loop to generate the rest: result[i-1] + result[i-2]
Solution: Start with [0,1], then push sum of last two numbers

title: Find Prime Numbers
description: Find all prime numbers up to a given number.
instructions: Create a function called `solution(max)` that returns an array of all prime numbers from 2 up to and including max.
hints: A prime number is only divisible by 1 and itself
Check each number from 2 to max
For each number, try dividing by all numbers less than it
If any division has no remainder, it's not prime
Solution: Use nested loops - outer for candidates, inner to check divisibility
